snowflakeWarehouse.title: How do I find my Snowflake warehouse?
snowflakeWarehouse.intro: A warehouse in Snowflake is a cluster of compute resources that executes queries and performs data loading operations.
snowflakeWarehouse.stepsIntro: Here's how to find your warehouse:
snowflakeWarehouse.step1: Log in to your Snowflake account and navigate to the "Compute - Warehouses" section in the left sidebar.
snowflakeWarehouse.step2: You'll see a list of available warehouses. Common default names include "COMPUTE_WH" or "PROD_WH".
snowflakeWarehouse.step3: Select the warehouse you want to use for this connection. Make sure it has the appropriate size and auto-suspend settings for your workload.
snowflakeWarehouse.step4: If you don't have a warehouse, you can create one using the "Create Warehouse" button or run: CREATE WAREHOUSE my_warehouse;

snowflakeUsername.title: How do I find my Snowflake username?
snowflakeUsername.intro: Your Snowflake username is the login identifier for your Snowflake account.
snowflakeUsername.stepsIntro: Here's what you need to know:
snowflakeUsername.step1: Use the same username you use to log in to the Snowflake web interface.
snowflakeUsername.step2: Snowflake usernames are case-insensitive and are typically in uppercase by default.
snowflakeUsername.step3: If you're using SSO (Single Sign-On) for the web interface, you may need to set a password or programmatic access token (PAT) for your user account, or ask your administrator to enable programmatic access.
snowflakeUsername.step4: You can view all users in your account by running: SHOW USERS; (requires appropriate privileges)

snowflakePassword.title: How do I manage my Snowflake PAT?
snowflakePassword.intro: Use a Personal Access Token (PAT) from your Snowflake account for authentication.
snowflakePassword.step1Prefix: To reset your PAT, go to
snowflakePassword.step3: PATs are encrypted and securely stored. They are never shown in plain text after saving.

snowflakePassphrase.title: What is a passphrase and when do I need it?
snowflakePassphrase.intro: A passphrase is an optional encryption password that protects your private key.
snowflakePassphrase.stepsIntro: Here's what you need to know:
snowflakePassphrase.step1: If you generated your private key with a passphrase (encrypted key), you must provide it here.
snowflakePassphrase.step2: If your private key is not encrypted (generated without the -nocrypt flag), leave this field empty.
snowflakePassphrase.step3: When generating an encrypted key with OpenSSL, you set the passphrase during the key generation process.
snowflakePassphrase.step4: The passphrase adds an extra layer of security by encrypting the private key file itself.
snowflakePassphrase.step5: This passphrase is only used to decrypt the private key and is never sent to Snowflake.

snowflakeKeyPair.title: How do I set up key pair authentication?
snowflakeKeyPair.content:
To use key pair authentication, generate an RSA key pair and configure your Snowflake user.

1. Generate an RSA key pair using OpenSSL:
openssl genrsa 2048 | openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -inform PEM -out rsa_key.p8 -nocrypt

2. Extract the public key:
openssl rsa -in rsa_key.p8 -pubout -out rsa_key.pub

3. Assign the public key to your Snowflake user as ACCOUNTADMIN:
ALTER USER your_username SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY='MIIBIjANBg...';

4. Copy the private key content from rsa_key.p8 into the Private Key field above.

snowflakeAuthMethod.title: Which authentication method should I choose?
snowflakeAuthMethod.content:
Snowflake supports two authentication methods:

Username & PAT (Programmatic access token): The simplest method using your Snowflake username and PAT. Suitable for development and testing.

Key Pair Authentication: A more secure method using public/private key cryptography. Recommended for production. Generate an RSA key pair and assign the public key to your Snowflake user.

snowflakeAccount.title: How do I find my Snowflake account identifier?
snowflakeAccount.content:
1. Open the account selector and review accounts you previously signed in to.
2. Select View account details.
3. The Account Details dialog shows the account identifier and account URL.
4. Copy the locator from the Account locator field.
5. Find the region in the account selector.
6. Combine locator and region as locator.region. Examples: xy12345.ap-northeast-3.aws or xy12345.north-europe.azure.

redshiftWorkgroup.title: What is a Redshift Serverless workgroup?
redshiftWorkgroup.content:
A workgroup is a collection of compute resources in Redshift Serverless. Use this field with Redshift Serverless. You can find the workgroup name in the Redshift Serverless Console.

Note: provide either a workgroup name (Serverless) or a cluster identifier (provisioned clusters), not both.

redshiftSecret.title: What is an AWS Secret Access Key?
redshiftSecret.content:
The Secret Access Key is the private part of your AWS security credentials. It is used with the Access Key ID to sign and authenticate AWS API requests.

Secret Access Keys are typically 40 characters long and shown only once when created. If you lose it, create a new access key pair.

Security warning: keep this key secure and never share it publicly. It is stored encrypted.

redshiftRegion.title: What is the AWS region?
redshiftRegion.content:
The AWS region is the geographic location where your Redshift cluster or Serverless workgroup is hosted.

Common examples:
us-east-1 - US East (N. Virginia)
us-west-2 - US West (Oregon)
eu-west-1 - Europe (Ireland)
ap-southeast-1 - Asia Pacific (Singapore)

Find the region in the AWS Redshift Console.

redshiftDatabase.title: What is the database name?
redshiftDatabase.content: The database name is the database you want to connect to inside your Redshift cluster or workgroup. Every cluster/workgroup has at least one database; the default is often dev. This field is required for all authentication methods.

redshiftCluster.title: What is a cluster identifier?
redshiftCluster.content:
A cluster identifier is the unique name of a provisioned Redshift cluster. Use this field for a traditional Redshift cluster, not Serverless. Find it in the Redshift Clusters Console.

Note: provide either a cluster identifier (provisioned) or a workgroup name (Serverless), not both.

redshiftAccessKey.title: What is an AWS Access Key ID?
redshiftAccessKey.content:
The Access Key ID is part of your AWS security credentials. It is used with the Secret Access Key to authenticate AWS API requests.

Access keys are typically 20 characters long and start with AKIA or ASIA for temporary credentials. Create them in the AWS IAM Console.

databricksToken.title: How do I generate a Personal Access Token?
databricksToken.content:
Personal Access Tokens (PAT) provide secure authentication to Databricks.

1. Sign in to your Databricks workspace.
2. Click your username and select User Settings.
3. Open the Developer tab.
4. Next to Access tokens, click Manage.
5. Click Generate new token.
6. Optionally add a comment and expiration.
7. Click Generate, then copy the token and store it securely; it will not be shown again.

Security: never share the token, set an expiration, revoke unused tokens, and use separate tokens per application.

databricksHttpPath.title: How do I find the SQL warehouse HTTP path?
databricksHttpPath.content:
The HTTP path identifies the SQL warehouse used for query execution.

1. Sign in to Databricks.
2. Open SQL Warehouses.
3. Select the warehouse.
4. Open Connection Details.
5. Copy the HTTP Path value.

Example: /sql/1.0/warehouses/abc123def456789

databricksHost.title: How do I find my Databricks workspace URL?
databricksHost.content:
The Databricks workspace URL is the hostname of your workspace. Copy the hostname from the browser address bar, before the first slash.

AWS example: dbc-12345678-90ab.cloud.databricks.com
Azure example: adb-123456789.7.azuredatabricks.net
GCP example: 12345678901234.5.gcp.databricks.com

googleBigQueryProject.title: How do I find my Project ID?
googleBigQueryProject.content:
This is the ID of your Google Cloud project. BigQuery usage costs are charged to this project.

1. Open Google Cloud Console and sign in.
2. Open the project selector.
3. Find the project; Project ID is shown in the ID column.
4. Use search if the project is not visible.

googleBigQueryServiceAccount.title: How do I get a Service Account JSON key?
googleBigQueryServiceAccount.content:
1. Open Google Cloud Console > IAM & Admin > Service Accounts.
2. Create a service account or select an existing one.
3. Grant bigquery.dataEditor and bigquery.jobUser roles.
4. Open Keys > Add key > Create new key.
5. Choose JSON and click Create.
6. Copy the downloaded file content into the field above.

googleBigQueryOAuth.title: What permissions will be requested?
googleBigQueryOAuth.content:
When you connect with Google, P2PDigital requests:

- BigQuery: read and write access to configured datasets and tables.
- Basic profile info: your name and email to identify the connected account.

P2PDigital only accesses BigQuery resources you configure as storage. You can revoke access from Google Account settings. The connected account needs BigQuery Data Editor and BigQuery Job User roles on the target project.

googleBigQueryLocation.title: How do I find my dataset location?
googleBigQueryLocation.content:
BigQuery data is stored in regions. Queries must process data in the same location to avoid errors.

1. Open the Google Cloud Console BigQuery page.
2. Expand your project and find your datasets.
3. Open a dataset and read the Data location field, such as US, EU, or asia-northeast1.
4. Keep datasets in the same location where possible.
5. Enter this location in the field above.

legacyGoogleBigQueryProject.title: Why can't I change the project ID?
legacyGoogleBigQueryProject.content: The project ID is fixed and cannot be changed. A separate system storage is created for each GCP project to keep compatibility with the P2PDigital extension for Google Sheets. Its project ID automatically matches the GCP project. Contact support if you need storage for another project.

legacyGoogleBigQueryLocation.title: How do I find my dataset location?
legacyGoogleBigQueryLocation.content:
Auto-detect location is selected by default. A specific location can improve stability. BigQuery queries must process data in the same region as the stored data.

1. Open the Google Cloud Console BigQuery page.
2. Expand your project and find your datasets.
3. Read the Data location field, such as US, EU, or asia-northeast1.
4. Keep datasets in one location where possible.
5. Enter the location in the field above.

athenaAccessKey.title: How do I get my AWS Access Key ID?
athenaAccessKey.content:
Before accessing an AWS Access Key ID, make sure an IAM user has the required Athena and Glue permissions.

The Access Key ID is part of the AWS credentials used to connect and authenticate.

1. Open the AWS IAM Security Credentials page.
2. Under Access keys, use an existing key or create a new one.
3. When creating a key, download and securely store both the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key.

athenaSecret.title: How do I get my AWS Secret Access Key?
athenaSecret.content:
The Secret Access Key is part of the AWS credentials used to connect and authenticate. It is shown only when a new key is created.

1. Open the AWS IAM Security Credentials page.
2. Under Access keys, create a new key if you do not have one or lost the secret.
3. Copy and securely store the Secret Access Key; it cannot be displayed again.

athenaRegion.title: How do I find my Athena region?
athenaRegion.content:
Athena queries run in a specific AWS region. Select the region where Athena and the data are located.

1. Open the AWS Athena console.
2. Read the selected region in the top-right region selector.
3. Enter the same region here to avoid connection or query errors.

athenaBucket.title: How do I find an S3 bucket?
athenaBucket.content:
Athena stores query results in an S3 bucket. Specify the bucket used for query output.

1. Open the AWS S3 console.
2. Select an existing Athena result bucket or create one.
3. A new bucket must be in the same region as Athena.
4. Enter the bucket name in this field.
